rows.speaker: علي بن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Hurayra says the sacred-state term literally includes ihram and entering the sanctuary, where hunting has the same ruling.
rows.anchor: حكم قتل الصيد فيهما على سواء بظاهر الآية , قاله علي بن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد، إبراهيم، ابن جريج
rows.claim: Intentional killing means deliberately killing game while forgetting that one is in ihram.
rows.anchor: متعمدا لقتله , ناسيا لإحرامه , قاله مجاهد , وإبراهيم , وابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء، الزهري
rows.claim: Intentional killing means knowingly killing game while remembering one is in ihram.
rows.anchor: متعمدا لقتله ذاكرا لإحرامه , قاله ابن عباس , وعطاء , والزهري

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: A person who accidentally kills game while forgetting ihram owes no compensation.
rows.anchor: لا جزاء عليه , قاله داود

rows.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: A person who accidentally kills game while forgetting ihram still owes compensation.
rows.anchor: عليه الجزاء , قاله مالك , والشافعي , وأبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The livestock equivalent is purchased with the value of the game killed.
rows.anchor: أن قيمة الصيد مصروفة في مثله من النعم , قاله أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The livestock equivalent must resemble the game in form and likeness.
rows.anchor: أن عليه مثل الصيد من النعم في الصورة والشبه قاله الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two learned, upright men determine the livestock equivalent, and the killer may serve as one of them.
rows.anchor: فلا يستقر المثل فيه إلا بحكم عدلين فقيهين , ويجوز أن يكون القاتل أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the offering to the Kaaba means delivering it anywhere in the sanctuary, since the Kaaba lies within it.
rows.anchor: وعنى بالكعبة جميع الحرم , لأنها في الحرم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Small sheep that are invalid for the sacrificial offering may not be offered in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: من صغار الغنم على قولين : أحدهما : لا يجوز قاله : أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Small sheep that are invalid for the sacrificial offering may still be offered in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يجوز , قاله الشافعي

rows.speaker: عطاء، الشافعي
rows.claim: For food expiation, value the livestock equivalent and buy food with that amount.
rows.anchor: أنه يقوم المثل من النعم ويشتري بالقيمة طعاما , قاله عطاء , والشافعي

rows.speaker: قتادة، أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: For food expiation, value the game killed and buy food with its price.
rows.anchor: يقوم الصيد ويشتري بالغنيمة طعاما , قاله قتادة , وأبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: عطاء، الشافعي
rows.claim: One fasting day substitutes for each mudd of food owed.
rows.anchor: أنه يصوم عن كل مد يوما , قاله عطاء , والشافعي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Three fasting days substitute for each mudd of food owed.
rows.anchor: يصوم عن كل مد ثلاثة أيام , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Two fasting days substitute for each saʿ of food owed.
rows.anchor: يصوم عن كل صاع يومين , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عامر، إبراهيم، السدي
rows.claim: The expiations are sequential: use livestock first, then food if no equivalent is available, then fasting if food is unavailable.
rows.anchor: على الترتيب , إن لم يجد المثل فالإطعام , فإن لم يجد الطعام فالصيام , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد , وعامر , وإبراهيم , والسدي

rows.speaker: عطاء، ابن عباس، الشافعي
rows.claim: The expiations may be chosen freely; this is Ata's view, one report from Ibn Abbas, and the Shafiʿi school's position.
rows.anchor: على التخيير في التكفير بأي الثلاثة شاء , قاله عطاء , وهو أحد قولي ابن عباس , ومذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offender tastes the consequence through the obligation to expiate and repent.
rows.anchor: يعني في التزام الكفارة , ووجوب التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pardon concerns acts committed before the prohibition was revealed.
rows.anchor: عفا الله عما سلف } يعني قبل نزول التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of recurrence is another killing after the prohibition, bringing immediate compensation and later punishment for the sin.
rows.anchor: يعني ومن عاد بعد التحريم , فينتقم الله منه بالجزاء عاجلا , وعقوبة المعصية آجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that the offender repeats the killing after an earlier one.
rows.anchor: ومن عاد بعد التحريم في قتل الصيد ثانية بعد أوله , فينتقم الله منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، داود
rows.claim: On the repeated-killing reading, God's retribution is afterlife punishment without another compensation.
rows.anchor: فينتقم الله منه بالعقوبة في الآخرة دون الجزاء , قاله ابن عباس , وداود

rows.speaker: الشافعي، الجمهور
rows.claim: On the repeated-killing reading, retribution includes both compensation and punishment.
rows.anchor: بالجزاء مع العقوبة ، قاله الشافعي ، والجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who forgot the reminders abandoned God's signs that establish His oneness and the truthfulness of His messenger.
rows.anchor: تركوا ما ذكرهم الله من آياته الدالة على توحيده وصدق رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened gates are worldly blessings and abundant provision.
rows.anchor: يعني من نعم الدنيا وسعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the blessings were meant to prompt the people to believe.
rows.anchor: ليكون إنعامه عليهم داعيا إلى إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the blessings were a form of gradual entrapment and a trial.
rows.anchor: ليكون استدراجا وبلوى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports the Prophet saying that continued gifts amid disobedience are a divine istidraj.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة ابن عامر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إذا رأيت الله يعطي العباد ما يشاءون على معاصيهم إياه فإنما ذلك استدراج منه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejoiced in the blessings they had received yet did not believe.
rows.anchor: يعني من النعم فلم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sudden destruction can be punishment for both their disbelief in God and their ingratitude for His blessings.
rows.anchor: أنه تعجيل العذاب المهلك جزاء لأمرين . أحدهما : لكفرهم به . والثاني : لكفرهم بنعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sudden taking means death arriving swiftly while they are heedless in their blessings, cutting off pleasure and intensifying regret.
rows.anchor: هو سرعة الموت عند الغفلة عنه بالنعم قطعا للذة , وتعذيبا للحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation of mublisūn is despair; ʿAdi ibn Zayd's المستبلس means the despairing person.
rows.anchor: ملك إذا حل العفاة ببابه … غبطوا وأنجح منهم المستبلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn can mean grief and regret.
rows.anchor: أنه الحزن والندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn can mean humility.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn can mean being forsaken.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الخذلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn can mean silence and the loss of an argument; al-ʿAjjāj's supporting line continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: والخامس : السكوت وانقطاع الحجة , ومنه قول العجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line attributed to al-ʿAjjāj supports reading أبلسا as silence or the loss of an argument.
rows.anchor: يا صاح هل تعرف رسما مكرسا قال نعم أعرفه وأبلسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects invoked besides God are idols.
rows.anchor: يعني الأصنام , وفي دعائها في هذا الموضع تأويلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking idols can mean worshipping them.
rows.anchor: في هذا الموضع تأويلان : أحدهما : عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking idols can mean seeking success from them.
rows.anchor: والثاني : طلب النجاح منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols do not own or control harm or benefit for their worshippers.
rows.anchor: قيل : معناه ما لا يملك لنا ضرا ولا نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning on one's heels after God's guidance means turning back after being guided to Islam.
rows.anchor: بالإسلام . { كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of being lured by devils can mean their calling someone to their way so he follows them, as in Abraham 14:37.
rows.anchor: أنه استدعاؤها إلى قصدها واتباعها , كقوله تعالى : ^ { فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم } ^ [ إبراهيم : 37 ] أي تقصدهم وتتبعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the devils command the person to fall into desire.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنها أمرها بالهوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and his wife inviting their son Abd al-Rahman to Islam and guidance.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس : أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر وامرأته حين دعوا ابنهما عبد الرحمن إلى الإسلام والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth by which God created the heavens and earth can mean wisdom.
rows.anchor: في الحق الذي خلق به السموات والأرض أربعة أقاويل : أحدها : أنه الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth by which God created the heavens and earth can mean beneficence toward His servants.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الإحسان إلى العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth can mean that the act of creating itself is real and true.
rows.anchor: والثالث : نفس خلقها فإنه حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth can mean the word of truth.
rows.anchor: والرابع : يعني بكلمة الحق

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: One view takes God's command Be to address the Day of Resurrection, which occurs without His repeating the command.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يقول ليوم القيامة : كن فيكون , لا يثني إليه القول مرة بعد أخرى , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another view takes the command to address the heavens, which become forms for the resurrection and are replaced by another heaven.
rows.anchor: أنه يقول للسموات كوني صورا ينفخ فيه لقيام الساعة , فتكون صورا مثل القرآن , وتبدل سماء أخرى , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is a horn blown first for annihilation and then for re-creation, marking the end and beginning, as in 39:68.
rows.anchor: أن الصور قرن ينفخ فيه النفخة الأولى للفناء , والثانية للإنشاء علامة للانتهاء والابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-ṣūr is the plural of image, into which its spirit is blown so it comes alive.
rows.anchor: أن الصور جمع صورة تنفخ فيها روحها فتحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knower of the unseen and seen may refer back to the creation of the heavens and earth; unseen is what is hidden from people and seen what they witness.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى خلق السموات والأرض , والغيب ما يغيب عنكم , والشهادة ما تشاهدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase refers back to the blowing of the trumpet, with God overseeing that blowing.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى نفخ الصور هو عالم الغيب والشهادة المتولي للنفخة

rows.speaker: الحسن، السدي، محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Hasan, al-Suddi, and Ibn Ishaq say Azar was Abraham's father's name.
rows.anchor: أن آزر اسم أبيه , قاله الحسن , والسدي , ومحمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies Azar as a man from Kutha, a village in the Sawad of Kufa.
rows.anchor: كان رجلا من أهل كوتى قرية من سواد الكوفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Azar was the name of an idol and Abraham's father's name was Tarakh.
rows.anchor: أن آزر اسم صنم , وكان اسم أبيه تارح , قال مجاهد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Azar is not a name but an insulting description meaning crooked, for turning away from truth.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس باسم , وإنما هو صفة سب بعيب , ومعناه معوج , كأنه عابه باعوجاجه عن الحق , قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's rebuke is justified because his father neglected God's right, which overrides a parent's right.
rows.anchor: لأنه سبه بتضييعه حق الله تعالى , وحق الوالد يسقط في تضييع حق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstratives ذا, ذلك, and ذاك distinguish near reference, distant reference, and emphasis of something distant.
rows.anchor: ذلك وذاك وذا : إشارات , إلا أن ذا لما قرب , وذلك لما بعد , وذاك لتفخيم شأن ما بعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation of the kingdom of the heavens and earth is their creation.
rows.anchor: أنه خلق السموات والأرض , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another interpretation is sovereignty, with Mujahid explaining that the word for kingdom is Nabataean.
rows.anchor: أن الملكوت هو الملك بالنبطية , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says kingdom is an Arabic formation like rahba/rahbūt and raḥma/raḥamūt; the proverb says fear is better than mercy.
rows.anchor: خير من أن نرحم , قاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the kingdom as the signs of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: معناه آيات السموات والأرض , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the kingdom with the sun, moon, and stars.
rows.anchor: هو الشمس والقمر والنجوم , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada specifies the heavens' moon, stars, and sun, and the earth's mountains, trees, and seas.
rows.anchor: أن ملكوت السماوات : القمر , والنجوم , والشمس , وملكوت الأرض : الجبال , والشجر , والبحار , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the certain may mean certainty of God's oneness and power.
rows.anchor: من الموقنين لوحدانية الله تعالى وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean certainty of Abraham's prophethood and the validity of his message.
rows.anchor: من الموقنين نبوته وصحة رسالته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the star Abraham saw was Venus, which rose at dusk.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : ذكر لنا أنه رأى الزهرة طلعت عشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night covering Abraham is glossed as covering or concealing him; related words for garden, jinn, madness, fetus, and shield likewise evoke concealment.
rows.anchor: ومعنى جن عليه الليل , أي ستره , ولذلك سمي البستان جنة لأن الشجر يسترها , والجن لاستتارهم عن العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hudhayli poetic line uses جنه for something covered by the dark dusk.
rows.anchor: وماء وردت قيل الكرى … وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that Abraham said this as a provisional supposition while reasoning.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : هذا ربي في ظني , لأنه في حال تقليب واستدلال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham actually believed the star was his Lord.
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك اعتقادا أنه ربه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the statement in Abraham's childhood, before proof and before a state in which belief or unbelief applied.
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك في حال الطفولية والصغر , لأن أمه ولدته في مغارة حذرا عليه من نمرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says he did not speak in belief but rejected idol worship: even greater heavenly bodies cannot be gods if they set, so handmade idols are less worthy.
rows.anchor: لم يقل ذلك قول معتقد , وإنما قاله على وجه الإنكار لعبادة الأصنام , فإذا كان الكوكب والشمس القمر وما لم تصنعه يد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view reads this as a rebuke in the form of a rhetorical question: Is this my Lord?
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك توبيخا على وجه الإنكار الذي يكون معه ألف الاستفهام وتقديره : أهذا ربي , كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting means disappearing; Dhu al-Rumma's line uses الآفلات for stars that set.
rows.anchor: أي غاب , قال ذو الرمة : مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not loving the setting stars means not loving them as a worshipped Lord; ordinary affection for them is unobjectionable.
rows.anchor: يعني حب رب معبود , وإلا فلا حرج في محبتهم غير حب الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāziġ means rising; the same word describes the sun when it rises.
rows.anchor: أي طالعا , وكذلك بزغت الشمس أي طلعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Setting proves celestial bodies cannot be worshipped because their change shows they are governed and originated, and what has that quality cannot be a deity.
rows.anchor: لأن تغيرها بالأفول دليل على أنها مدبرة محدثة , وما كان بهذه الصفة استحال أن يكون إلها معبودا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: One interpretation of what lacks God's name is animals the Arabs sacrificed to their idols.
rows.anchor: ذبائح كانت العرب تذبحها لأوثانها , قاله عطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation is carrion.
rows.anchor: أنها الميتة , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says it means game caught by polytheists who do not invoke God; Muslims may not eat it unless they themselves hunted it.
rows.anchor: لا يذكرون اسم الله , ولا هم من أهل التسمية , يحرم على المسلمين أن يأكلوه حتى يكونوا هم الذين صادوه , حكاه ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is any animal over which God's name was not spoken at slaughter.
rows.anchor: أنه ما لم يسم الله عند ذبحه

rows.speaker: الحسن، الشافعي
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Shafiʿi say omission of the name does not prohibit eating, whether deliberate or forgetful.
rows.anchor: لا يحرم [ سواء ] تركها عامدا أو ناسيا , قاله الحسن , والشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says deliberate omission prohibits eating, while forgetful omission does not.
rows.anchor: يحرم إن تركها عامدا , ولا يحرم إن تركها ناسيا , قاله أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين، داود
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin and Dawud say omission prohibits eating whether deliberate or forgetful.
rows.anchor: يحرم سواء تركها عامدا أو ناسيا , قاله ابن سيرين , وداود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Fusq means disobedience.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به المعصية , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fusq can also mean sin.
rows.anchor: والثاني : المراد به الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' whispering to their allies concerns argument over slaughter and food.
rows.anchor: يعني المجادلة في الذبيحة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the devils were Persians who wrote to their Quraysh allies challenging Muhammad's followers for rejecting carrion while eating their own slaughter; the verse was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: ويأكلون ما ذبحوه لأنفسهم , فأنزل الله تعالى فيهم هذه الآية , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says the devils said this to their allies among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: أن الشياطين قالوا ذلك لأوليائهم من قريش , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says a group of Jews said this to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أن قوما من اليهود قالوا ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' revelation to their allies can mean signaling them.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنها إشارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can mean sending them a message.
rows.anchor: والثاني : رسالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying them makes people polytheists in the matter of carrion if they declare it lawful.
rows.anchor: يعني في أكل الميتة , إنكم لمشركون إن استحللتموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle in Iblis's statement can mark an oath: By Your causing me to err, I will sit in wait.
rows.anchor: على معنى القسم وتقديره : فبإغوائك لي لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it marks recompense: Because You led me astray, I will sit in wait.
rows.anchor: على معنى المجازاة , تقديره : فلأنك أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ighwaytani means You led me astray.
rows.anchor: معناه أضللتني , قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is You deprived me of Your garden; a poet's يغو means to be disappointed.
rows.anchor: ومن يغو لا يعدم على الغي لائما أي ومن يخب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ighwaytani can mean You punished me, as in Maryam 19:59, where ghayy means punishment.
rows.anchor: معناه عذبتني كقوله تعالى : ^ { فسوف يلقون غيا } ^ [ مريم : 59 ] أي عذابا , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further meaning is You destroyed me by cursing; the phrase غوى الفصيل describes a young camel nearing death from lack of milk.
rows.anchor: معناه أهلكتني بلعنك لي , يقال غوى الفصيل إذا أشفى على الهلاك بفقد اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accompanying poem uses ميت غوى for the young animal close to death from lack of milk.
rows.anchor: معطفة الأثناء ليس فصيلها … برازئها درا ولا ميت غوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's pledge is to sit in wait on God's straight path.
rows.anchor: أي على صراطك المستقيم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the path as the Meccan road, where Iblis would deter people from pilgrimage and umrah.
rows.anchor: طريق مكة ليصد عن قصدها في الحج والعمرة , قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets it as the path of truth, from which Iblis would mislead people.
rows.anchor: طريق الحق ليصد عنها بالإغواء , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: From before means sowing doubt about the afterlife; from behind means tempting people with worldly life; from the right means through good deeds; from the left through bad deeds.
rows.anchor: أيمانهم } : أي من قبل حسناتهم , { وعن شمآئلهم } من قبل سيئاتهم , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي، إبراهيم
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibrahim read before as worldly life, behind as the afterlife, right as casting doubt about truth, and left as tempting toward falsehood.
rows.anchor: وعن أيمأنهم } : الحق أشككهم فيه , { وعن شمائلهم } : الباطل أرغبهم فيه , قاله السدي وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the front and right are directions people can see, while behind and left are directions they cannot see.
rows.anchor: من حيث ينظرون , { ومن خلفهم } { وعن شمائلهم } : من حيث لا يبصرون , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: A later scholar says Iblis meant every direction available for deception; mercy blocks approach from above, and below is omitted to avoid repulsion.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر من فوقهم لأن رحمة الله تصده , ولا من تحت أرجلهم لما فيه التنفير , قاله بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth possibility: before means the remaining lifespan, behind the past lifespan, right one's wealth, and left one's poverty, each exploited to deter obedience or repentance.
rows.anchor: فيما بقي من أعمارهم فلا يقدمون على طاعة , { ومن خلفهم } : فيما مضى من أعمارهم فلا يتوبون عن معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth possibility: before means extended hopes, behind entrenched ignorance, right whatever is easy, and left whatever is difficult.
rows.anchor: بسط أملهم , { ومن خلفهم } تحكيم جهلهم , { وعن أيمانهم } : فيما ييسر لهم , { وعن شمائلهم } : فيما تعسر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungrateful may mean those who fail to thank God for His blessings.
rows.anchor: شاكرين لنعمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean those who do not remain obedient to God.
rows.anchor: والثاني : مقيمين على طاعتك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One answer is that Iblis only guessed, and his guess proved true in 34:20; after misleading Adam, he assumed Adam's descendants would be weaker.
rows.anchor: قال : ذرية هذا أضعف منه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that Iblis could have learned it from the angels through information from God.
rows.anchor: أنه يجوز أن يكون علم ذلك من جهة الملائكة بخبر من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested water can mean water of mercy, and the requested provision can mean spiritual closeness to God.
rows.anchor: من ماء الرحمة ومما رزقكم الله من القربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the water means water of life and the provision means worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: من ماء الحياة ومما رزقكم الله من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good land is land with good soil.
rows.anchor: يعني طيب التربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With its Lord's permission, the good land grows fine, good vegetation.
rows.anchor: يعني يخرج نباته حسنا جيدا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says n-akad means little growth from which no benefit is gained.
rows.anchor: أن النكد القليل الذي لا ينتفع به , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that n-akad means difficult and harsh, preventing good; a poet uses المنكود and الناكد for this sense.
rows.anchor: أنه العسر بشدته المانع من خيره , قال الشاعر : وأعط ما أعطيته طيبا لا خير في المنكود والناكد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي
rows.claim: The good and barren lands exemplify the believer as good earth and the disbeliever as salty, bad earth.
rows.anchor: للمؤمن والكافر , فجعل المؤمن كالأرض الطيبة والكافر كالأرض الخبيثة السبخة , قاله ابن عباس , والحسن , ومجاهد , وقتادة , والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The council called al-malāʾ may mean Pharaoh's notables.
rows.anchor: الملأ من قوم فرعون } فيهم ثلاثة أقاويل : أحدها : أنه أشرافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead mean Pharaoh's leaders.
rows.anchor: والثاني : رؤساؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies them as the group or party who believed with them.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أنهم الرهط والنفر الذين آمنوا معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One distinction between rahṭ and nafar is that the former is larger and the latter smaller.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين الرهط والنفر من وجهين : أحدهما : كثرة الرهط وقلة النفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another distinction is that rahṭ is stronger and nafar weaker.
rows.anchor: والثاني : قوة الرهط وضعف النفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malāʾ may be called so because its members are capable of what is asked of them.
rows.anchor: أنهم مليئون بما يراد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their awe fills people's hearts.
rows.anchor: لأنهم تملأ النفوس هيبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that they fill the seats of meeting places.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يملأون صدور المجالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They objected despite worshipping Pharaoh because his conduct departed from the normal royal practice of crushing open defiance; this was God's favor to Moses.
rows.anchor: لأنهم رأوا منه خلاف عادته وعادة الملوك في السطوة بمن أظهر العناد وخالف , وكان ذلك من لطف الله بموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Moses and his people would corrupt the land can mean worshipping someone besides Pharaoh and calling people away from his religion.
rows.anchor: ليفسدوا فيها بعبادة غيرك والدعاء إلى خلاف دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means taking control of the land and wresting it from Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: ليفسدوا فيها بالغلبة عليها وأخذ قومه منها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Pharaoh worshipped idols while his people worshipped him, explaining the reference to his gods despite his claim in 79:24.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يعبد الأصنام وكان قومه يعبدونه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh worshipped favorite cows; this explains why the Samiri made a calf and said it was the god of the people and Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال هذا إلهكم وإله موسى , وكان معبودا في قومه , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Pharaoh's people worshipped idols to draw near to him.
rows.anchor: أنها كنت أصناما يعبدها قومه تقربا إليه , قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the phrase as and your worship, rather than and your gods.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس { ويذرك وإلاهتك } أي وعبادتك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Pharaoh both worshipped and was worshipped, so the wording raises no difficulty.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : وكان فرعون يعبد ويعبد . وعلى هذه القراءة يسقط السؤال

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba offers another reading explanation: ilāha means the sun, which Arabs called al-ilāha, and he cites al-Aʿshā.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن قتيبة في هذه القراءة تأويلا ثانيا ؛ أن الإلاهة الشمس , والعرب تسمي الشمس الإلاهة
